summary: Embedding sequence-hash rotation causing intermittent candidate drop from rerank results
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using our rerank endpoint intermittently observe missing high-scoring candidates for a subset of queries. The symptom started after a scheduled scaling change to the embedding ingest service (sequence-hash sharding adjustment).

Impact:
- AtlasSearch reported ~0.6% of queries returning fewer than expected top-K candidates, typically the top 1-3 missing.
- Observable across two regions (us-east primary, eu-west replica).
- Causes downstream quality regressions for search/QA features; revenue-impacting for AtlasSearch production traffic.

Environment:
- Prod embedding ingest pipeline run with embed-v2.
- Reranker service reranker-v1 reading from ANN index built from ingested embeddings.
- Autoscaling/reshard event executed 2026-03-12 03:12 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (internal repro):
1. Rebuild test index with same ingest config used during scaling (sequence-hash mod N).
2. Send curated query set used by AtlasSearch (attached) to rerank endpoint (topK=50).
3. Compare candidate IDs returned to baseline index built without the recent hash rotation.

Observed behavior:
- A reproducible subset (~2% of queries in test set) miss previously present candidates. Missing candidates correlate with embedding IDs whose sequence-hash changed bucket assignment after the reshard.
- Logs show successful ingestion but lookup for some IDs during ANN scan returns null or stale cache misses followed by fallback to lower-quality candidates.

Expected behavior:
- Resharding/sequence-hash changes should be handled without candidate omission: either a transparent rekey/backfill or consistent lookup via aliasing.

Relevant logs/metrics:
- Ingest pipeline traces show no ingestion errors; commit offsets indicate writes succeeded.
- Cache-miss rate spiked during reshard window: cache_miss_rate_embed_lookup +540% (03:10-03:20 UTC).
- ANN query logs show KeyNotFound events for specific ID prefixes matching rotated hash range.

Immediate workaround provided to customer:
- Rolled back the sequence-hash mod parameter for AtlasSearch tenant to previous value and triggered a controlled backfill for the affected namespace. This restored expected candidate sets for repro queries.

Notes on sensitivity:
- No evidence of data corruption; appears to be key-routing/namespace aliasing issue introduced by sharding change.
comments: 2026-03-13 09:22 - Priya Desai (Support): Customer reported missing top results after our maintenance window. Provided initial logs and sample queries. Escalating to SRE/infra.

2026-03-13 11:05 - SRE on-call (Daniel Chen): Observed cache-miss spike around reshard time. Hypothesis: deterministic sequence-hash parameter changed, causing lookups to target different shard keys. Starting deeper trace across ingest and ANN lookups.

2026-03-13 13:40 - Eng (Marta Alvarez): Confirmed lookup KeyNotFound pattern for IDs that were rehashed. Repro locally by toggling hash modulus. Creating PR to add alias mapping during reshard to avoid lookup gaps.

2026-03-13 16:10 - Priya Desai (Support): Notified customer of temporary rollback and requested verification. Customer confirmed improved results for their repro set; still monitoring production traffic.

2026-03-14 08:30 - Liam O'Connor (Assignee): Implemented hotfix in staging that introduces a multi-key lookup fallback and a short-lived alias table. Running extended regression and preparing rollout plan for prod with backfill window.

2026-03-14 12:00 - AtlasSearch (Customer contact: Raj Menon): Provided long query log showing missing candidate IDs. Asked for ETA on permanent fix and whether historical backfills will be complete within 24 hours.
investigation_notes: 03/13 11:10 - Correlated missing candidates with sequence-hash namespace rotation triggered by autoscaling rule change. The mod parameter used in the ingest service changed from 128 to 256 during the rollout.
03/13 12:15 - ANN index build assumed stable ID->shard mapping; index shards were not rebalanced to include new key ranges immediately, leading to lookups against incorrect shards.
03/13 12:45 - Cache design relied on direct shard-key resolution; when hash rotates, cached keys are not aliased, producing KeyNotFound until backfill completes.
03/13 13:50 - Confirmed no write failures; data for affected IDs exists in storage but is unreachable via current lookup path without alias mapping.
03/14 08:00 - Code path review: ingest client uses sequence_hash(id) % N for routing. Rerank lookup used a runtime-configured N that got out of sync for short window during the rollout.
resolution: Hotfix rolled to prod 2026-03-14 10:45 UTC: (1) added alias table that maps legacy shard keys to current shard keys during transitions, (2) fallback multi-key lookup in ANN service to query both old/new keys for 24h grace, (3) started background backfill job to rebuild affected ANN partitions and populate cache. Backfill completion ETA: 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC for AtlasSearch tenant. Follow-up: implement an automated aliasing mechanism in ingest control plane and add a preflight check to prevent unsynced runtime-mod parameter changes. Patch PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/4821.
postmortem_followup_tasks: Implement preflight validation for hash-mod parameter changes (owner: infra-team, due: 2026-03-20)
Add automated alias mapping in control plane during reshard operations (owner: storage-team, due: 2026-03-18)
Create monitoring alert for KeyNotFound events exceeding baseline (owner: observability, due: 2026-03-16)
Run audit for other tenants who received same reshard flag during maintenance window (owner: support/ops, due: 2026-03-15)
